svg.title: The same loop in two languages
svg.desc: Two panels, each summing the list 1 2 3 4 5 with an explicit loop, and each printing 15. Left, J: a five-line explicit definition opened with 3 colon 0, using local assignment, a for_i. loop and a closing parenthesis on its own line, then called as sumloop 1 2 3 4 5; the caption says you had to leave the ordinary notation to write this, and the idiom is two characters, plus-slash. Right, q: x colon 1 2 3 4 5, r colon 0, i colon 0, then one line, do count x, r plus-colon x i, i plus-colon 1, then show r; the caption says it is one line of ordinary q that looks like every other line, and the idiom is sum. The footer says: a language that lets you stay comfortable will not teach you a paradigm shift; go where the shift is unavoidable, then come back.
svg.text: Neither language forbids the loop. Only one makes it feel foreign.

g.text: for_i. y do. r =. r + i end.

svg.text: Five lines of visibly foreign machinery.
A new definition form, a different assignment,
Ordinary q, like every line around it.
to land. It doesn't look like a detour.
A language that lets you stay comfortable will not teach you a paradigm shift. Go where the shift is unavoidable, then come back.
